name: Mannerism
summary: Elongated, twisting figures in crowded, unstable space, in acid colour. The painters took the Renaissance rules and bent them on purpose: grace and artifice replace calm balance.

philosophy.core_thesis: A picture is most beautiful when it shows skill and invention, so the painter stretches, twists and crowds the ideal body past nature.
design_principles: Draw the figure 9 to 10 heads tall, with a small head and long limbs and neck.
Twist each figure in a serpentine line (figura serpentinata) that spirals up through 180° or more.
Fill the picture to the edges with 5–15 figures, and leave no calm floor to stand on.
Tilt the space: raise the horizon and push the ground up the picture plane so that figures climb and stack.
Use acid, shifting colour: a cold pink, lemon, green and blue that change hue inside one drape (cangiante).
Light the figure from a cold, unclear source, and keep the faces smooth and enamel-like.
Put the main action off to one side or far back, and place a large decorative figure in front.
anti_patterns: Calm, symmetric balance around a central axis
Figures of natural proportion, 7 to 8 heads tall
Clear, deep perspective with an open floor
Warm, earthy colour that stays one hue in each drape
Empty space around the main figure

composition.layout: A crowded, vertical stack of twisting figures that climb the picture plane, with a raised horizon and a small, tilted window of deep space far behind.
composition.focal_point: A group of figures off-centre, at about one third from an edge; the eye is led there by a spiral of limbs and drapery.
composition.format: A tall panel or canvas at ratios of 2:3 to 1:2; the figures reach and are cut by the top and side edges.

principles.rule: Draw figures 9 to 10 heads tall, with the head at one tenth of the height, against 7 to 8 heads in the earlier ideal.
Repeat a spiral of limb and drapery 3–5 times from the base to the top, each turn 90° to 180° from the last.
Compress the space to 3 tight layers with a high horizon at 20–30% from the top, and a small deep gap behind.
Hold an unstable balance: put 60–70% of the figure mass on one side, and counter it with a small, far, bright figure.
Spread 4–5 acid hues across the figures in patches of 5–15% each, and keep no hue as a dominant field.
Place the main group at one third from the edge, and make it the only area where three or more diagonals meet.

palette.strategy: Cold, acid and shifting colour: a pink, lemon, sea-green and lapis blue, with a changing hue inside one fold of cloth, on a dark, cool ground.
palette.distribution: Flesh and pale drapery 35–45%, acid colour patches 30–40%, dark ground and shadow 20–30%.
palette.ground: A dark grey-green or brown ground, glazed with thin colour over a light underpainting.

brushwork_and_medium.medium: Oil paint with glazes over a pale tempera underpainting; in a wall picture, fresco.
brushwork_and_medium.support: Panel or fine-weave canvas with a smooth, pale ground.
brushwork_and_medium.brushwork: Fine strokes of 1–3mm, blended away; the hand does not show.
brushwork_and_medium.paint_handling: 4–8 thin layers with smooth glazes; the flesh is polished and the drapery is crisp and sharp.
brushwork_and_medium.edges: Hard, clean contours on the figures, with a soft edge only inside the hair and the far haze.

light_and_modelling.light: A cool, even or unclear light from a high side; it shows no warm sun and no strong beam.
light_and_modelling.modelling: Smooth, enamel-like skin with 4–6 steps from light to dark; the limbs read as cool marble.
light_and_modelling.shadow: Dark, cool and clean, kept to 15–25% of a figure; it does not blur the contour.
light_and_modelling.temperature: A cool key overall, with the warm tones kept to a small flesh or a red accent.

subject.typical: Religious scenes, myth and allegory, and long-necked portraits of court figures in stiff, rich dress.
subject.figure_scale: The figures fill 70–90% of the picture height and press the edges.
subject.treatment: Elegant, cool and artificial; the sitter or saint is poised, with no plain emotion on the face.

surface.finish: Smooth and glossy, polished like enamel.
surface.texture: No visible brush texture; a fine, even surface.

reference_works.note: Object ids were checked against the Art Institute of Chicago API (CC0 data). The third work is a drawing and shows the stretched figure. Look at the museum page for the image and its licence.

emotion.target_response: Unease and admiration: the viewer sees great skill and feels a cool, tense elegance that is not at rest.

use_cases: book and album covers with a strange, cold grace
portrait with a stylised, courtly look
avoid_when: The brief needs calm, plain clarity or a friendly mood.
The picture needs natural body proportion or a clear, open space.

modifiers.how: Reset the figure to 7 to 8 heads, bring back a central axis and an open floor, and use warm, one-hue drapery.
Keep the twist and the figure scale; cut the acid colour, add one strong beam of light and a dark ground at 50% of the area.

sources.title: Art Institute of Chicago API (CC0 data)
Giorgio Vasari, Lives of the Most Excellent Painters, Sculptors and Architects (1550)
